title: POV: You're a WhatsApp Message Travelling From New York to Mumbai 🌊 #shorts
description:
What really happens when you hit send? Your message is end-to-end encrypted on your phone, then sent to a WhatsApp server that can't read it but knows where it's going. From there it travels as pulses of light through fibre-optic cables laid on the ocean floor, comes ashore at a cable landing station, crosses Indian networks to a mobile tower, and reaches your friend's phone, which is the only device that can unlock it. More than 12,000 km, in well under a second. Undersea cables carry the vast majority of international internet traffic.

📘 More to learn + my projects: https://github.com/HemashreeVI

#WhatsApp #Internet #UnderseaCables #Networking #Tech #TechExplained #shorts

lines: POV: you're a WhatsApp message. It's 11:30 PM in New York, and Aarav just typed happy birthday.
First, you get locked. End-to-end encrypted into gibberish only one phone on Earth can open.
You race to a WhatsApp data centre. The server can't read you. It only knows where you're going.
Then you dive. Into a fibre-optic cable lying on the ocean floor, travelling as pulses of light.
Thousands of kilometres later, you come ashore at a cable landing station.
Through Indian networks, to a mobile tower near her home.
Her phone unlocks you. Happy birthday. Two blue ticks.
More than twelve thousand kilometres. Under an ocean.
